Was the holdout separated in time, or at random?

Source: R/checks-validation.R
validation_strategy_check.Rd

A random split asks whether the model can predict a row it has not seen. An out-of-time split asks whether it can predict next period, which is what a deployed model will be asked to do. Seasonality, inflation and portfolio mix all leak backwards through a random split.

Usage

validation_strategy_check(
  config = validation_config(),
  compliance = compliance_config()
)

Arguments

config

A validation_config().

compliance

A compliance_config().

Value

A gate_check.

Details

So model_card$validation_strategy is required, must be one of accepted_validation_strategies, and for a high-risk use case (any of compliance_config()'s high_risk_use_cases appearing in model_card$use_case) must be out of time. Blocking.

This is the one validation check that cannot be verified from the data. It records a claim, which is what a model card is for. Port of ValidationStrategyCheck in bdp-model-gate 0.7.0.

Examples

card <- list(use_case = "credit_scoring", validation_strategy = "random_split")
report <- run_gate(gate_context(data.frame(x = 1:3), model_card = card),
                   list(validation_strategy_check()))
report$results[[1]]$detail
#> [1] "credit_scoring is high-risk and was validated with a 'random_split' split - a random split cannot tell you whether the model holds up on next period's business, which is what it will be applied to"
